RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

An all-female panel alone is not evidence of gender bias, and alleging discrimination on that basis is legally unfounded and likely to harm your academic career. 

Lecturer appointments frequently prioritize teaching approach, interview performance, and departmental needs over publication counts alone. The successful candidate’s "strong experience from industry" was likely considered a compelling asset for teaching applied economics courses. 

Rather than focusing on panel demographics, follow up politely regarding your requested feedback. Frame your inquiry around constructive professional development to learn how you can strengthen future applications. Raising accusations without documented evidence will not change the hiring outcome and will only burn professional bridges.
